concepts.title: The Cell as the Unit of Life

questions.q: Why is the cell called the basic unit of life?
questions.a: All living things are made of cells, and every life function happens inside cells.

questions.q: Who discovered the cell and how?
questions.a: Robert Hooke, in 1665, seeing box-like rooms in cork under his microscope.

questions.q: What did Schleiden and Schwann propose?
questions.a: The cell theory - all living things are made of cells, and the cell is life's basic unit.

concepts.title: Cell Structure: Membrane, Nucleus and Organelles

questions.q: Name three parts of a typical cell.

questions.a: It holds chromosomes (DNA) and controls all the cell's activities.

questions.q: Which cell part releases energy from food?
questions.a: Mitochondria - the powerhouse of the cell.

concepts.title: Observing Cells with Microscopes and Scales

questions.q: Who invented the microscope and what did it reveal?
questions.a: Anton van Leeuwenhoek improved microscopes and revealed tiny living 'animalcules' (microbes).

questions.q: What is the use of a compound microscope in cell study?
questions.a: It magnifies cells hundreds of times so their parts can be seen.

questions.q: Why do we stain cells before observing them?
questions.a: Stains colour the thin transparent parts, making nucleus and structures clearly visible.
